title: Task-contrast wiring alignment in 176 IBL mouse regions was sensitive to the spatial null
abstract: We tested whether input wiring follows differences among five task-coding maps after broad spatial patterns are removed. We used 176 IBL mouse brain regions, Knox connection density and Allen CCF geometry. After ten broad modes were removed, a joint spectral sign reference gave alignment excess 0.01923, p = 0.0037 and Holm p = 0.0111. Technical features showed no excess. Removing forty modes removed the task-contrast excess while 59% of its squared norm remained. On maps with no wiring term, unequal local amplitude and a nonlinear mean gave sign-test rejection rates of 16.5% and 22%. We then used conditional Gaussian residual rotations for raw scores, repeated all rank transforms per draw, and tested 22 fixed non-wiring spatial covariance shapes with quadratic mean controls. Their p values ranged from 0.0069 to 0.8007. The finite union was not rejected. Matching-model checks gave 5.5% and 2.5% rejection; a covariance mismatch gave 10.5%. The rotation extension was developed after the sign-test failures. A conditional proof, original code, source hashes, aggregate draws and figures are supplied. These tests show spatial-reference sensitivity. They do not show that wiring has no effect or refute earlier tests with different statistics. One common dataset, limited Gaussian models, rounded scores, no cell-mix test and no measurement-error resampling limit the result. External raw and derived regional databases are not bundled.

display.caption: Task-contrast excess falls with removal of spatial modes. The spectral reference can be liberal under unequal local amplitude and a nonlinear mean. Conditional Gaussian rotation results change across 22 non-wiring spatial covariance shapes. Error bars in the calibration panel are 95% Wilson intervals.

Observed alignment and the joint spectral reference after ten broad modes are removed. The grey ranges are null reference ranges, not biological confidence intervals. All task, task-contrast and intrinsic endpoints have an excess, but technical features do not. Sign invariance is an assumption, not a consequence of matching power.
